text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success, and it starts with the SMART framework. This means your goals should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," you could say "increase user sign-ups by 20% within three months." Once you have this overall goal, you break it down into smaller milestones, which are key checkpoints along the way. Each milestone leads to a concrete deliverable, such as a completed design or a final report. Crucially, you must ensure stakeholder alignment from the beginning. This means talking to everyone involved early on to confirm they agree with the goals and understand their role. When everyone is on the same page, you can track progress effectively and avoid wasted effort.
